title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts there is a block that decides whether a changed target file
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts there is a block that decides whether a changed target file has a test. It currently guesses two filenames and reports the target as untested when neither exists. Extend it so a test that lives under a different filename still counts. One file.

The block to extend begins with this line, which occurs exactly once and is indented with six spaces:
      const candidates = [

Leave the existing two guessed paths and the loop that checks them with access() completely unchanged. They are correct whenever they hit. Add a second chance that runs ONLY if that loop finished without finding anything, so this can never lower the number it reports.

Implement the second chance as simply as possible, using one directory read rather than a hand-written recursive walk:

1. From the target path, which looks like repos/<vessel>/src/<rest>, build the vessel test directory path repos/<vessel>/test, joined onto the same root the existing code already computes.
2. Call readdir on that directory with the recursive option set to true, inside a try so a missing directory simply means no second chance.
3. Keep only entries whose name ends in .test.ts, and stop after the first two hundred.
4. Read each such file and look for the target module being imported.

For step 4 the test is a string containment check against the module basename, and it must match a WHOLE path segment. Build two needles from the basename: a forward slash followed by the basename followed by a double quote, and a forward slash followed by the basename followed by .js and a double quote. Treat the target as covered if a file contains either needle. Repeat both needles with single quotes.

That whole-segment requirement is the point of the change, so do not relax it into a plain substring or prefix test. For a module named gap the specifier ending /gap or /gap.js counts; a specifier ending /gap-lifecycle-scan must not. A prefix test would report coverage for modules a test never loads, and this count feeds the recovery ladder rung that claims landed changes are known to do something, so an over-reporting check makes that rung state something false. Under-reporting is the safe direction here.

Wrap the entire second chance so that any thrown error leaves the result as not covered.

Evidence this is needed: the most frequently rewritten file in this vessel is reported as having no test, while three test files exist whose names begin with its basename, and exactly one of them actually imports it. An import check counts that one and correctly ignores the other two, which a filename check would have miscounted.

Do not alter the branch taken when a guessed path exists, do not change the warning message or any counter, and edit no other file.
